- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/api/v1/meta (route, 36 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **24** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e22315238f9426708e10cfff1d6a96e56cca33a1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fdf8fbff1516569e6c4b10fe5e8206930043230c` — the merge of head `caeb7b58f1a0f6a207d0036b73788c19be28595f` into base `e22315238f9426708e10cfff1d6a96e56cca33a1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin fdf8fbff1516569e6c4b10fe5e8206930043230c && git checkout fdf8fbff1516569e6c4b10fe5e8206930043230c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e22315238f9426708e10cfff1d6a96e56cca33a1 caeb7b58f1a0f6a207d0036b73788c19be28595f && git checkout -B drift-repro e22315238f9426708e10cfff1d6a96e56cca33a1 && git merge --no-ff caeb7b58f1a0f6a207d0036b73788c19be28595f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e22315238f9426708e10cfff1d6a96e56cca33a1
```

</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e22315238f9426708e10cfff1d6a96e56cca33a1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `caeb7b58f1a0f6a207d0036b73788c19be28595f`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #22591 (body; triage 6093105279; claim 6093560675 as amended; os-dev-reports 6094519413 and 6094616222), PR #22623 (body, its six-file list, the net diff against `main` at `e22315238f`), and the check-runs on this head. Nothing was built, run or re-run; the source cited below was read through the API at the head or the base sha, never from a checkout.

### ① Derived judgments

Public surface of `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` (its `exports` map has the `.` entry only, and `index.ts` does not re-export `packaged-base-regime.ts`, so `managedItemSealedSentence` and the new `SealedItemOperation` type stay internal):

- `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.packagedBaseRefusal` — `operation` widens from `'save' | 'delete'` to `'save' | 'create' | 'delete'`. An additive input on an exported class's method; every existing call compiles unchanged. **Right**, and the widening the declaration names.
- `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.tenantAuthoredWriteRefusal` — gains an optional `operation` (`'save' | 'create'`), read as `'save'` when absent. Additive. **Right.**
- `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.saveMetaItem` — no signature change. Behaviour: a save whose `parentVersion` is a present `null` is handed to both locked-base doors (the flow rule and the package door) as a `create`, so its `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE` sentence names the create remedy; every other save is an edit as before. The reading is the door's standing contract, not a new inference: `packages/rest/src/meta-save-request.ts` maps `If-None-Match: *` to `parentVersion: null` ("no row of this lifecycle is here", the first-write pin), and `saveMetaItem`'s own text already says a `null` "says that save is a create: the state `If-None-Match: *` asserts". **Right.**

Accept set:

- Which writes are refused, and with which code and status, moves on no door. `refusePackagedBaseOverride` reads `operation` for the sentence and nothing else; `isSealedManagedItem` and the limbs before the sentence are untouched; `heldPositionNameRefusal` keeps the `save` predicate. The new pin asserts a `create` is refused exactly where a `save` is, with `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` / 403, on every reachable type on both kernel shapes (the registry's types with no overlay channel, asserted equal to the `allowOrgOverride` flag, plus a plugin-registered type; floor 20, 24 reached), and that a free name is `null` for both acts. **Right — no accept-set change, so `yes` carries no narrowing arm and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed.**
- An edit (`save`) and a removal (`delete`) keep their sentences byte for byte: the `save`/`delete` path of `managedItemSealedSentence` is unchanged, and `regimeCPrescription` now reads the same ADR path through the `REGIME_C_ADR` constant (declared after the function, read only at call time; no module-load hazard). **Right.**
- `heldNameSentence` is ONE sentence for every type; only the opener (an origin-gated row's noun, else "provided by a managed package") and the citation (ADR-0126 for Regime C, the row's `docs` for origin-gated, ADR-0131 otherwise) come from the row. It names no source artifact, no sanctioned path and no `OS_METADATA_WRITABLE` hatch, and the pin holds it under the REST door's 500-character bound with an 88-character name on every type. **Right** — the measured choice the card and triage left to the claimant (one create-aware sentence rather than a `position` row), and it closes the family instead of a fourth type. One wording observation, unpinned and owing no action: for an origin-gated name the host owns (`datasource/default`) the create opener reads "is code-defined" where the edit sentence names the host's configuration; the remedy kind is right either way.
- `canonicalizeMetaRequestType` spreads the request, so `folded.operation` reaches the sentence in both methods; the ablation of the one `create` line reads red in both suites (5 and 3 failures), which pins that path as load-bearing.

`@objectstack/plugin-security` (its `exports` map has the `.` entry only, and `index.ts` does not re-export `position-write-through.ts`, so `PositionMetadataDoor` is internal):

- `heldPositionNameRefusal` asks the door with `operation: 'create'`. At this head it is called at exactly two sites — a created row, and a `PATCH` whose `pre.name !== post.name` — and an edit that keeps a held name stands down before it, so no edit can receive the create remedy through Setup. The verdict it relays is the door's `save` verdict. **Right**; this is the producer of the card's measured symptom, named in the amended claim.
- The `PositionMetadataDoor.packagedBaseRefusal` member type widens to match; the real door satisfies it, and no published type moves.

Tests against the triage pin (6093105279): `protocol.sealed-remedy-kind.test.ts` is the enumeration pin asked for — every reachable type read off the registry, never a transcribed list, for an edit and a create, asserting the remedy KIND off what the sentence points at (the row's own routes or source read from the table, the redeploy remedy, or the type's listing route), with controls for the verdict, a free name, a removal and the 500-character bound, plus the `/meta` first-write versus unpinned versus `If-Match` rows for `position` and `flow` with the door's message equal to the verdict's (one emitter). `position-write-through.test.ts` pins the Setup create under a package-held name and a built-in (`everyone`), a rename into `guest`, and the S10 relay now against the door's first-write save, with the door's edit refusal as control. A type added to the registry later is iterated the day it lands. **Right.**

Docs: no page under `content/docs` restates the edit sentence the diff keeps or the create remedy it adds; `permissions/authorization.mdx` prescribes the package-source remedy for a posture edit of a sealed permission set, which is an edit and keeps its sentence. The Docs Drift Check's six rows name `saveMetaItem` and the class, not the sentence. No doc edit owed.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes

- Declared `yes` on PR body line 2 and in `.changeset/22591-sealed-remedy-kind.md`; the arm is absent, which `clause2-line.mjs` reads as the same widening as `yes (widening)`. It matches the diff: a public method's input domain grows (`packagedBaseRefusal` accepts `'create'`; `tenantAuthoredWriteRefusal` takes an optional `operation`), the accept set does not move, and nothing an author can write is removed or renamed — so no narrowing arm, no ADR-0087 marker and no migration mapping is owed.
- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: minor` — **right**: a widening takes at least `minor`.
- `@objectstack/plugin-security: minor` — **right in what it publishes, over-graded on its own surface**. Its published dist changes (the sentence Setup relays on a create), so a changeset is owed. Graded on its own surface it is a `patch`: no exported type of the package moves, and the gate's level axis would have accepted `patch` beside `metadata-protocol`'s `minor` (its `discharged` state exits 0, printing the residual). Both packages sit in the one fixed release group, so the bump that ships is `minor` for both whichever word the changeset carries; the declaration is not wrong about what ships, and no change is owed. `Check Changeset` is green on this head, both runs.
- `skip-changeset` is not used, correctly. The changeset body names every door the create remedy reaches and the FROM → TO of the sentence.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every deviation and open question in 6094519413 and 6094616222, and the amended claim's clauses:

1. File surface beyond the claim's two `protocol.ts` sites. (a) `plugin-security` `position-write-through.ts` and its test — covered by the claim amendment (6093560675) naming them as the producer side, declared to `domain:services`. Answered. (b) `tenantAuthoredWriteRefusal` plus the `saveMetaItem` first-write derivation — within the card's ask (the `/meta` door is where the card measured the sentence), and without it a flow would be the one type the first-write pin missed. Answered, right.
2. `sys-metadata-repository.ts` unchanged against the claim's file surface — its callers are server replays of the item's own stored history (draft promotion, restore, revert), all edits with no create fact to pass. Answered, right.
3. The changeset also bumps `plugin-security` — right (its dist moved; see ②).
4. `Clause-②` copied as `no` with `patch` in round 1 — superseded by patch round 1 at this head (`yes`, `minor` for both). The PR body's declaration line and its Acceptance-notes bullet both read `yes` now, and the gate-count paragraph is labelled as `3c3e4ef362`'s. Closed.
5. Merged `origin/main` `18d999031b`; built eight unrelated packages so `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` could measure; suites sequenced under one verify-lock call with per-part exits captured — local process notes with no bearing on the diff. Noted.
6. `open_questions[0]`, `yes (widening)` versus `no` — the seat answered A in the amended claim and the dev applied it at `caeb7b58f1`. Judged right: a new accepted value on an exported class's method is the widening the declaration asks about. Closed.
7. Round-2 deviations: the bare `yes` spelling (accepted; one reading), `check-changeset-fixed.mjs` run beyond the derivation (fine), PR CI not read by the dev (read here, below). Closed.
8. `out_of_scope_findings[0]` — **escalated to the seat; action owed**: Studio's create form (objectui `ResourceEditPage` create path) sends no `If-None-Match: *`, so after this PR an unpinned `PUT /api/v1/meta/position/NAME` from Studio still receives the edit remedy. The server half is this PR; the client half is an objectui card (send `If-None-Match: *` on create; `MetadataClient` needs the option), blocked by #22623 and back-linked to #22591. Not yet filed. Not a defect of this diff.
9. `out_of_scope_findings[1]` (`POST /automation` keeps the clone/switch remedy — by that door's own contract a create onto an existing name is an overwrite, and the clone door refuses a taken target name first) and `[2]` (code-only types are refused by `codeOnlyOverrideError` before the package door, right for a create too) — agreed, no carrier.
10. Claim clauses: "Stop on a breach" — none reported; the serial constraint (PR #22582 on `main`) was cleared at claim time; the #15206 S5 read-path regions are untouched. Governed surfaces: none in the file list (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green); this record is owed by the claim's widening clause, not by a Tier S path. The PR is still a draft; the seat flips it when it lands.

Check-runs on `caeb7b58f1`, read at 2026-10-10T06:47Z: 41 runs, all completed — 36 `success`, 5 `skipped` (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke, and Auto Label plus Check PR Size on the re-triggered run; each skip is a path filter, not a verdict), 0 pending, 0 failed, cancelled or timed out. Green by name: Build Core; Test Core 1/6–6/6 and the aggregate; Lint & Repo Gates; Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger) and TypeScript Type Check; Check Changeset (both runs); Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL); Dogfood Regression Gate 1/3–3/3 and the aggregate; Dogfood Verify CLI; Governed Surface Queue Guard; Flag docs affected by code changes; Check Documentation Links; the card-claims-branch, part-of, same-issue and single-writer guards (two runs each); filter. These conclusions are the gate verdicts; nothing was re-run here.
